claims.text: CI runs uv sync --locked, npm ci and npm run build in frontend, ruff check, ruff format --check, pytest, the no-data guard and a gitleaks scan of all history.
med-ask search returns passages with their book, PDF page and printed page.
The generated answer comes from a separate request that the browser posts after the evidence is shown.
The app is a Flask app that serves a built React front end.
The index is a LlamaIndex PGVectorStore on Postgres with pgvector.
Models are reached through Home Lab's gateway, whose base URL and key come from the environment, over the external homelab-models network.
CI verifies the export units with systemd-analyze verify.
CI's Compose job builds the stack and starts it with docker compose up.
The Compose job fetches the search page title and checks that /api/health returns postgres ok and vector ok.
The Compose job checks that public answers private and unknown API paths with 404, that app answers the private ping, and that no cloudflared container exists.
The app Compose service turns private routes on and publishes port 8100 on APP_BIND_ADDRESS.
The public service uses the same image as app, and its environment does not enable private routes.
The public service defines no ports.
The public service and cloudflared share the tunnel network.
The ingest service runs python -m med_ask.ingest under the ingest Compose profile.
cloudflared is the Cloudflare Tunnel connector and runs only under the tunnel Compose profile.
The postgres service runs the pgvector Postgres 17 image and defines no ports.
postgres holds the bookkeeping and question-log tables that Database.ensure creates.
The front end is a React 19 and Vite project built with vite build.
The Dockerfile builds the front end, copies it into the runtime image as FRONTEND_DIST, and the Flask app serves it.
The resolve and label APIs are registered only when private routes are enabled, which Compose does only in app.
Navigation is built by the ingest command navigate and read by app and public, which mount it read-only.
Retrieval evaluation runs inside the ingest command as its eval subcommand.
deploy/med-ask.service pulls main and then runs docker compose up with a build.
deploy/med-ask-export.service runs the question export, and its timer fires daily.
LlamaIndex's PGVectorStore owns the vector table, named per index, with hybrid search and approximate (HNSW) indexes disabled.
PyMuPDF reads PDF page text, bookmarks and page images.
Every model call goes through the OpenAI client with a purpose in the model field.
langdetect detects language using only the English, Spanish and Catalan profiles.
Gunicorn serves the Flask app with two workers.
med-ask's own tables hold bookkeeping, the question log and the translation cache.
Ingestion extracts passages, probes the endpoint's model and dimensions to choose the table, and inserts only missing passage ids through LlamaIndex.
A search logs the question, embeds it once, and retrieves passages and, from v5, figures.
Each candidate is sent to the grade purpose and only those graded yes are shown, grouped by book.
The answer route sends only the numbered passing passages to chat, validates the reply and returns it marked generated.
Review source loads page images from /api/page, and navigation supplies contents and evidence links.
On the server, med-ask.service runs Compose from the clone at /srv/homelab/med-ask after pulling main.
Data paths come from environment variables and fall back to named volumes when unset.
Page reading uses the vision purpose through the same MODEL_BASE_URL as every other purpose.
embed-large-bulk is a purpose name that the index-table rule knows alongside embed-large.
app, public and ingest join the external homelab-models network and call the gateway at MODEL_BASE_URL.
med-ask.service is part of homelab-data.target and orders itself after homelab.service, which it wants.
MODEL_BASE_URL defaults to http://litellm:4000/v1 and MODEL_API_KEY to unused, and the services join the external homelab-models network.
The model field carries the embedding purpose from EMBEDDING_PURPOSE, grade, chat, translate and vision.
The reported embedding model selects the vector table name.
The reported dimensions are validated against the selected table's recorded dimensions, and a mismatch is refused.
med-ask's units depend on the /srv/homelab mount, homelab-data.target and homelab.service.
Both units carry ConditionPathIsMountPoint=/srv/homelab.
Outside private mode the app takes the asker from the Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email header.
The image contains both the built front end and the API.
The Access email header is read only when private routes are off, as in public.
public defines no ports.
Compose passes environment settings to app, public, ingest, postgres and cloudflared.
POSTGRES_PASSWORD has no default, and Compose stops with a message when it is unset.
Compose gives the bind address, the data paths, the index version, the embedding purpose and the embedding roles a default when they are unset.
The export writes one row_to_json row of medask_questions per line.
The export units run ingest export-questions, which writes /data/originals/questions.jsonl.
Database.ensure creates the tables if missing and adds missing question-log columns.
app, public and ingest all connect to the postgres service.
The schema is medask_models, medask_books, medask_questions and medask_translations plus LlamaIndex vector tables, and init.sql creates the vector extension.
Columns are added with ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS under an advisory lock that serializes the two app services.
The claims file declares version 1, and the checker asserts it.
The claims file names this repository as the one it documents.
The link test checks that every path and line the claims file cites exists.
The link test requires unique ids per kind in the claims file.
The postgres service publishes no port and stores data in POSTGRES_DATA_PATH, defaulting to the postgres-data named volume.
postgres/init.sql, mounted as an entrypoint init script, only creates the vector extension.
CI's Compose job removes its volume with docker compose down -v when it ends.
The app reads DATABASE_URL and an optional FRONTEND_DIST from the environment.
Private routes are enabled only when PRIVATE_ROUTES_ENABLED equals exactly true.
The sources directory is mounted at /data/sources read-only and holds the PDFs and books.toml.
The originals directory, mounted at /data/originals only in app and ingest, holds readings, resolutions, exports and eval files.
The navigation directory is mounted at /data/navigation, read-write only in ingest.
Postgres data is mounted at /var/lib/postgresql/data.
The image runs as UID and GID 10001.
The manifest is books.toml in the sources directory, in the format of books.example.toml.
Book ids must be unique lowercase URL-safe identifiers and filenames PDF basenames that stay inside the sources directory.
The optional eval_book is a unique, non-empty eval-set id for the book.
Routes look books up by id in the manifest rather than by a supplied path.
Compose refuses to start without POSTGRES_PASSWORD.
APP_BIND_ADDRESS defaults to loopback; on the server it is the private Tailscale IPv4 address.
Unset data paths fall back to the postgres-data, sources-empty, originals-empty and navigation-empty named volumes.
COMPOSE_PROFILES and TUNNEL_TOKEN are empty by default, so no tunnel runs.
INDEX_VERSION, EMBEDDING_PURPOSE and EMBEDDING_ROLES default to v2, embed and false.
med-ask.service is part of homelab-data.target and is installed into it.
med-ask.service orders itself after Docker, Tailscale and homelab.service, and wants homelab.service.
homelab-models is an external network, and the unit only runs when /srv/homelab is already a mount point.
The export timer fires daily at 03:00 and Persistent=true catches up missed runs.
The export runs only while /srv/homelab is mounted and med-ask.service is active.
The export runs ingest with --no-deps and --pull never, mounting the clone's src read-only and selecting it with PYTHONPATH.
The export streams rows into a temporary file in the same directory and atomically replaces questions.jsonl.
With fewer rows than the existing file the export refuses, exits 1 and leaves the file untouched.
The export reads only medask_questions, not the translation cache.
Each start runs a fast-forward pull of main whose failure is ignored, then docker compose up --build.
Stopping the unit runs docker compose down without removing volumes.
app, public and ingest all use the med-ask-local image.
/api/health returns postgres ok and vector ok when the vector extension exists, and HTTP 503 otherwise.
app and public run the same image, and both serve the page and /api/health.
With private routes off every /api/private/ path returns the unknown-route 404.
public mounts only sources and navigation and publishes no port.
cloudflared joins only the tunnel network, which public shares and app and postgres do not.
cloudflared uses the tunnel profile, and CI asserts no cloudflared container exists.
The connector's command is tunnel --no-autoupdate run and TUNNEL_TOKEN comes from its environment.
With private routes off, the asker is the Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email header.
Without NAVIGATION_PATH the navigation mount falls back to the navigation-empty volume.
homelab-models is declared external, so Compose does not create it.
Ingest asks the store which ids exist, skips them and inserts the rest one passage at a time.
status reports stored current ids, extracted counts and duplicate gaps per book for every recorded table.
Search raises No index yet when the current model has no table.
Page reading skips complete kept readings, the description job skips kept records, and ingest skips stored ids.
Each index table is named e_<version>_<model stem>_<model hash>, and the store's table carries the data_ prefix.
The table's stem and hash come from the model the endpoint reports.
INDEX_VERSION must be v followed by one to four digits.
medask_models records each table's model and dimensions; ingest refuses a different recorded model and search refuses a missing or different one.
EMBEDDING_ROLES enables roles only when it equals true.
With roles on, questions carry input_type query and passages input_type passage through extra_body, with unchanged text.
Role tables add r after the version, except for embed-large and embed-large-bulk.
A passage id hashes the book id, the PDF page range and the unchanged text.
Below v5 the index holds passages only, of every kind in the extraction vocabulary.
In v5 the index adds figure nodes of kind figure whose text is the printed label and caption, with Passarge plates kept whole.
From v6 the index splits Passarge plates into lettered panels, as v5 otherwise.
Search returns only content, summary and glossary passages, whatever INDEX_VERSION is.
EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT defaults to 20 seconds.
The vector store creates its table when opened with setup, and Database.register and book_count record a table's model and book counts.
Compose passes INDEX_VERSION, EMBEDDING_PURPOSE and EMBEDDING_ROLES to app, public and ingest.
The served version comes from INDEX_VERSION in the environment, defaulting to v2.
Extraction runs without network access and returns plain records in memory with an account of every PDF page.
A passage's text source is born-digital, inherited-ocr or ocr.
Hidden placeholder pages produce no passage, are skipped by reading, and block joins across them.
Extraction applies owner resolutions before separating captions and headings.
A passage's kind comes from the nearest recognised heading in its section path, ignoring case and whitespace, defaulting to content.
Passage ids hash only book, pages and text, and all metadata including kind is excluded from embedding text.
Ingest stores every node, while search filters to content, summary and glossary.
Contents and index sections are excluded in text layers and readings using the same titles.
A new chapter or front-matter heading closes the prior section, while repeated headers of the same chapter keep its subsection.
Reading headings are kind titles, chapter and numbered section titles, PDF-confirmed headings, or short uppercase or title-case lines of at most 14 words and 120 characters.
Matching PDF heading sizes set the hierarchy, otherwise headings use one peer level.
Without readings legacy boundaries are kept, and each reading paragraph becomes one passage.
Reading lines have the preview-watermark words Copyrighted material removed, while the adjoining text and numbers stay.
Sustained repetition of a 1–64-token pattern in eight copies over 64 tokens and 200 characters, or 200 copies of one horizontal whitespace character, cuts the tail.
Reading passages keep their failed rules as check_page and ocr_reasons, and the browser labels them from OCR — check the page.
Unfinished content sentences join the next passage in the same book and section when it starts lower case or ends hyphenated, removing the hyphen.
Only pages without body passages may lie between joined passages, and none may be hidden.
The page-join pass excludes inherited OCR, readings that failed a rule, and every kind but content.
Without kept readings, the legacy paragraph reassembly can still join inherited-OCR text across pages, as a synthetic scanned page followed by a born-digital page shows.
A joined passage's PDF and printed ranges are extended across the join.
Publisher text is kept except for nearly empty pages with ink.
Language, word-shape and number checks apply only to readings and inherited OCR.
Hidden placeholders fail no rule and are skipped by the reader.
The reason codes are empty-ink, language, nonwords, number-missing, number-order, token-limit and page-timeout.
The thresholds are constants in ocr.py; the ink test renders the inner page at 72 DPI and needs over 0.1% of pixels below intensity 180.
The ocr and ocr-queue commands read the manifest and skip the database.
--limit caps the number of new pages read per book.
The queue summary lists failing pages and hidden, kept, read-and-passing and queued totals, reading seconds, rotations, rescues and word-shape quantiles, without book text.
Pages are sent one at a time as in-memory PNGs at 300 DPI, temperature 0, at most 4,096 tokens and a 180-second timeout.
The transcription prompt keeps printed language and spelling, joins hyphenation, separates paragraphs and replaces figure interiors with [FIGURE n] and the caption.
An upright reading is retried once rotated 180 degrees only for empty-ink, nonwords or page-timeout; a timeout is saved as an empty attempt.
The kept reading prefers completed replies, then the fewest failed rules, then upright.
A connection failure or HTTP 5xx stops the run with exit code 3 without saving a failed reading.
Readings are saved at /data/originals/ocr/<book-id>/<pdf-page>.json with the selected text, model, method version, rotation, failed rules, seconds, time and every attempt.
Readings are written to a synced temporary file and renamed atomically.
Files of another METHOD_VERSION are ignored and kept as previous versions, and current-version attempts are not repeated.
ocr-recheck recomputes rules and finalizes partial readings without model calls, and ocr runs the same recheck before reading.
Figure entries use captions extraction separated: [FIGURE n] markers in readings and Figure, Figura or Fig. paragraphs in text layers.
Each figure keeps its label, caption, book, PDF and printed page, and its id hashes source identity and occurrence.
A figure node's text is its label followed by its printed caption, ignoring descriptions.
Grading sends a figure's caption text and printed label, and answers receive only numbered texts.
PASSARGE_PLATES is the even PDF pages 32–420 except 244 and 274, plus pages 422–426.
A plate's label is its printed title and its caption the facing legend; the maps use PDF 422's title and PDF 421's legend.
Extraction refuses a Passarge PDF that lacks the settled plate pages.
Passarge entries keep pdf_page for the plate and legend_pdf_page for the caption; nodes cite the legend page and store figure_pdf_page for the plate.
A passage whose text contains a plate's printed title links that plate.
From v6 ordinary plates split into panels at lettered headings, labelled title plus letter, while unlettered plates and maps stay whole.
A panel's opening text is kept only when it has at most PASSARGE_OPENING_LIMIT characters and at most a third of the panel's text.
A legend passage links the one panel containing it, otherwise all of that plate's panels in letter order.
From v5 search retrieves figures separately with the same embedding and appends them after the passages.
FIGURE_CANDIDATES, defaulting to 4, caps the figures a search returns.
Half of the figure slots go to direct figure matches first.
Then figures referenced by the retrieved passages in the same book fill slots in passage order, and unused slots go to further direct matches.
Figure-number references in prose are matched by the REFERENCE pattern.
figures-count reports figures, captionless and unnumbered counts per book without a model.
figures-describe renders the whole page at 300 DPI, sends it with label and caption in one vision call, and saves a generated record under /data/originals/figures.
Reruns skip kept records including failures, timeouts are failures, and an outage stops the run.
Extraction leaves descriptions unread by default, and descriptions are removed before evidence reaches storage or the browser.
/api/search accepts a question of 1–4000 characters after NUL removal.
The question is logged before search, and a missing index still finishes the log row.
Search retrieves PASSAGE_CANDIDATES passages, defaulting to 26, and from v5 figures, then sends each candidate to grade.
Grading runs in parallel up to GRADE_CONCURRENCY (default 15), each call with GRADE_TIMEOUT defaulting to 6 seconds.
Only a complete yes or no counts, other replies and errors are ungraded, and calls have no retries.
Compose's application environment sets none of the grading or candidate variables.
While a search runs the screen says checking which passages answer this….
Only yes-graded candidates are kept, grouped by book in similarity order with books ordered by their best passage and numbers running across books.
The search response holds question_id, language, evidence, groups, not_found, ungraded_count and embedding, grading and search seconds.
When nothing passes the screen shows Not found. These books don't cover the question. and the answer route refuses without evidence.
Evidence carries labels, language, section, OCR provenance, links and at most the two same-section neighbours, each capped at 120 words.
The source label adds summary or glossary kinds.
Inherited OCR or check_page passages say from OCR — check the page, and other readings say from OCR.
The page route renders the PDF page about 1000 pixels wide to PNG in memory with a private one-hour Cache-Control.
The browser posts question_id to /api/answer, which sends chat only the question and numbered passing passages.
The answer prompt requires at most 150 words in the question's language, citations on every sentence, and gaps, disagreements and thin support stated.
Answers must be JSON sentences with valid citations, one sentence each and at most 150 words; failures return an error without touching the evidence.
The Generated answer panel is rendered before the evidence and labelled generated.
Language detection uses local English, Spanish and Catalan profiles and falls back to English.
Translation is available only when a passage's language differs from the question's.
/api/translate takes question_id and a displayed passage_id, sends that original alone to translate and returns it marked generated.
Translations are cached in medask_translations by passage id and language, and a cached reply returns cached true before any endpoint is built.
Purposes other than grade use GENERATION_TIMEOUT, defaulting to 20 seconds.
medask_questions holds question, asker, time, language, vector table, evidence, grades, ungraded count, answer and feedback.
Each request path calls ensure, which creates tables and adds missing columns.
Answer and translation use only evidence whose logged grade is yes, so rows without grades have no evidence to answer from.
The export writes whole medask_questions rows and no translation rows.
With private routes on the asker is tailnet; otherwise it is the Access email header, and a missing header is a 401.
Question, answer and feedback lookups match both the id and the asker.
No asker identity is in a grade message, which carries only the question, the passage text and a figure's label.
No asker identity is in an answer message, which carries only the question and the numbered passage texts.
No asker identity is in a translation message, which carries only the translation instruction and the passage text.
Feedback accepts thumbs up, down or null and a comment of at most 4000 characters, with NUL removed.
The eval file defaults to /data/originals/eval/med-ask-eval.v2.jsonl, overridable by EVAL_FILE, with results in runs/ beside it unless EVAL_RUNS_DIR is set.
Manifest eval_book values map books to eval ids, and unmapped eval books count as not indexed.
The eval runs the app's search, whose table follows INDEX_VERSION, with PASSAGE_CANDIDATES as k.
--purpose defaults to EMBEDDING_PURPOSE and --roles/--no-roles override EMBEDDING_ROLES.
Only confirmed records are scored by default, and --status is repeatable.
An eval run calls only search, writes a new run-<time>-<purpose>-roles-<on|off>-<suffix>.json exclusively, and stores ids, scores, ranks, pages and timings.
Comparison output treats a missing roles field as off.
Figures are removed from results before scoring, and runs record ranking_scope passages.
A passage hits when any page in its inclusive PDF range is a confirmed page of the eval book.
Only confirmed evidence for indexed books with page text counts, and answerable records without it are skipped.
The summary gates on Hit@5 over scored questions and reports Hit@10, Hit at the cut, work coverage at 10 and Hit@5 by language, type, subject and book.
Embedding time is the median and slowest of the first 20 questions after one fixed-text warm-up.
Not-found questions are not scored, and their top similarity is reported beside answerable questions'.
Malformed records are reported by id or line and retired records are not run.
Compare arguments without a slash are looked up in the runs directory.
A candidate passes when total Hit@5 does not drop and lost hits are balanced by gained ones.
Comparison prints lost and gained ids, exits 0 on pass and 1 on fail, and refusals such as different set versions exit 2.
The figure gate accepts only a v4 baseline with a v5 candidate, or a v5 baseline with a v6 candidate, whose tables carry those versions.
The figure gate requires eval set version 2, the embed-large purpose and roles off in both runs.
A v5 and v6 pair must also rank passages only, with ranking_scope passages.
Both runs must score the same 32 ids, and the 20 cohort ids must be among them.
The baseline must reach Hit@10 32 overall and 20 on the cohort, or the gate refuses.
The candidate passes only when it also reaches Hit@10 32 overall and 20 on the cohort.
The gate reports Hit@5 and Hit@10 overall and for the cohort.
Real-case modes read REAL_EVAL_FILE or the default real-case labels, and exit 0 with Nothing labelled yet when empty.
Served mode builds no endpoint and recovers candidates by node id from the recorded vector_table in logged rank order.
In served mode a log without grades is reported unscorable with reason logged before grading.
Candidates without recovered pages are counted as unresolved.
End-to-end mode reruns search and grading without generating answers or changing labels or logs.
In-scope results report returned, passed, hit10 and hit at the cut, and served mode counts every logged candidate for the cut.
Out-of-sources results report correct_not_found when nothing passed and list wrongly_passed ids.
Each real-case result records its table and its count of candidates with no grade.
navigate writes /data/navigation/<book-id>.json with version, fingerprint, contents, pages and references, without model calls.
Only ingest mounts navigation read-write.
The fingerprint covers the PDF, readings, resolutions and builder code; a change mid-build refuses publication, and files are replaced atomically.
Loading checks only the version, book and PDF stat, caching per worker until the file or PDF changes.
Loading navigation never extracts a book.
The contents and page routes return contents or page info with page_count, 404 when navigation is unavailable or out of range, and evidence links are empty without navigation.
The book viewer fetches page info and the page image and renders the contents tree.
References are counted per kind: figure, table, section, chapter and page.
Every kind whose seeded precision is below 90 percent is removed from references and recorded in excluded_kinds.
The report's precision_passed requires overall retained precision of at least 90 percent.
Books whose readings supply more than half the content pages keep only numbered chapter and section headings, attached to observed chapters without inventing any.
The navigation report is counts only and holds a seeded precision sample and contents coverage.
The report marks contents as thin when they have fewer than two levels or cover under half the content pages.
The report's chapter_entry_coverage marks chapter numbers 1 through the highest observed one by whether a chapter entry exists, which is a diagnostic and not a verified total.
The resolve blueprint is registered only with private routes on, and the screen's button shows only then.
Without private routes every /api/private/ request returns 404 before routing, and public has no originals mount.
Resolve writes with a different Origin header are rejected.
resolve-cache accepts book ids, uses no model or database, and writes diagnostics.json per book atomically.
The cache build refuses to publish when its inputs changed during inspection.
A missing or stale cache raises DiagnosticsUnavailable with the rebuild command, which the API returns as 503.
The cache fingerprint covers the PDF and kept readings but not resolutions, a hint advances only its reading's entry, and workers reuse the parsed cache until the file changes.
The queue route accepts book and reason filters and omits resolved pages.
The page route returns the page's reading record, printed number and reason messages.
A resolution action is confirm, number with printed_page, text with text, or hinted with attempt_id.
A hint adds the owner's text to the prompt in one vision request with a 20-second timeout and no retries, and returns 503 when vision is not serving.
A hinted attempt is appended to the reading's history without being selected, returned as generated, and accepting it saves a resolution.
Resolutions are per-page files under /data/originals/resolutions with an appended, timestamped history.
Resolution writes hold an exclusive per-book file lock.
Extraction applies the latest resolution and clears its failures, and the queue skips resolved pages.
Saving a resolution only writes its file and answers that it applies at the next rebuild.
Only the app, with PRIVATE_ROUTES_ENABLED equal to true, registers the label blueprint, and the front end shows Label questions only when the private ping answers.
The list filters logged questions by inclusive dates, newest first, and the detail returns question, date, language and logged answer.
Suggestions put passing logged candidates first, then other logged ones, then a k=100 search, each book page once.
Logs without grades recover their evidence ids from the recorded index with no grade.
The wider suggestions route only calls search.
A label is unlabelled without a record, out of the sources when expect_not_found, otherwise in scope; outside and clear empty the pages.
The label routes are /questions with from and to, /question/<id>, its /suggestions, and POST /label with add, remove, outside or clear; page actions need book_id and pdf_page.
Label requests are limited to 32,000 bytes, cross-origin POSTs are rejected, and responses are no-store.
Labels are saved under a directory lock by rewriting and atomically replacing the real-case file, keeping other records and dropping a cleared one.
A label record has schema 1, status confirmed, unclassified type and subject, the log's question and language, id r plus 12 hex digits, and log_id.
A null log language is detected locally and marked detected; otherwise the source is log.
Evidence uses manifest eval_book ids with confirmed PDF pages, and outside records set expect_not_found with no evidence.
Search returns the original passages, with book and page, and the generated answer is requested afterwards.
Search results carry the book, the PDF page and the printed page.
Each candidate is sent to the grade purpose, and only candidates graded yes are shown.
The generated answer is limited to 150 words and the browser shows it under a Generated answer heading, apart from the sources.
A figure node's text is its printed label followed by its printed caption.
Opening a figure opens Review source at the plate or page, which the page route renders whole.
Navigation links figure, table, section, chapter and page references, and a reference opens a quick look.
Review source opens the book viewer with breadcrumbs and a contents tree.
Scanned pages are read through the vision purpose.
Doubtful pages are marked from OCR — check the page: inherited-OCR passages and readings that failed a rule carry that label.
Gunicorn serves the Flask app, the built React 19 and Vite interface and the API from one image.
PyMuPDF reads the pages.
LlamaIndex's PGVectorStore holds the index in Postgres with pgvector.
Models are called by purpose in the model field through an OpenAI client whose base URL and key come from MODEL_BASE_URL and MODEL_API_KEY.
The chat, embed, grade and vision purposes are named in code.
The services join the external homelab-models network that Home Lab provides.
The browser shows the Generated answer panel separately from the source list.
The no-data guard rejects tracked data extensions and forbidden directories, and CI runs it.
Tests use synthetic content: a test builds its PDF at runtime in a temporary path.
Indexes are named with INDEX_VERSION.
A new index is judged by the comparison gate, which passes a candidate only when total Hit@5 does not drop and lost questions are balanced by gained ones.
A label record takes its question from a logged question.
The project requires Python 3.13 or later, and CI uses Python 3.13 and Node 24.
The local checks are the uv, pytest, ruff, no-data guard, npm and gitleaks commands that CI runs.
The guard lists tracked files with git ls-files, and the front-end build output directory dist is git-ignored.
The .env.example file holds a password placeholder, .env is git-ignored, and the Docker context excludes everything it does not list.
The app is published on port 8100 of APP_BIND_ADDRESS, which defaults to loopback.
The health route returns postgres ok and vector ok when Postgres answers and the vector extension exists, and HTTP 503 otherwise.
Unknown /api/ paths return 404 with an Unknown API route error.
The public service takes the asker from the Cloudflare Access header and is reached through cloudflared.
Private routes are on only in app, which publishes on APP_BIND_ADDRESS.
The Flask app lives in src/med_ask.
The React interface and its Vite build live in frontend.
The systemd service and timer units live in deploy.
The repository check scripts live in scripts.
The database initialization script lives in postgres.
The automated tests live in tests.
The README diagrams are light and dark SVG files in docs/diagrams.
The licence is AGPL-3.0, as the LICENSE file and the AGPL-3.0-only project metadata state.

relations.text: app calls Home Lab's gateway by purpose at MODEL_BASE_URL over the homelab-models network.
public calls Home Lab's gateway by purpose at MODEL_BASE_URL over the homelab-models network.
ingest calls Home Lab's gateway by purpose at MODEL_BASE_URL over the homelab-models network.
app connects to postgres over the backend network with DATABASE_URL and uses its tables.
public connects to postgres over the backend network with DATABASE_URL and uses its tables.
ingest connects to postgres over the backend network with DATABASE_URL and uses its tables.
cloudflared shares only the tunnel network with public and forwards Access-protected requests to it.
The front end is served by the Flask app and calls its /api routes.
The search route calls retrieval's search with the purpose embedding endpoint.
The app calls generation to grade candidates, group evidence, write answers and translate.
The ingest and status commands call retrieval's ingest_book and ingest_status.
The eval command runs evaluation's run_eval with the app's own search.
The ocr commands call extraction's reading, re-checking and queue functions.

ingest_book extracts a book's passages and figures before it indexes them, while ingest_status extracts them only to count and compare stored ids and indexes nothing; the ingest and status commands call them.
The navigate command builds navigation files.
The app reads published navigation files from the read-only navigation mount.
With private routes on, the app registers the resolve and label blueprints.
The resolve API uses the OCR module's rules, readings and vision endpoint.
med-ask.service starts the Compose stack, including app, with docker compose up.
The export service runs ingest export-questions with the clone's source mounted read-only.
med-ask.service runs only on the mounted /srv/homelab volume, as part of homelab-data.target, after homelab.service.
The export service runs only while /srv/homelab is mounted and med-ask.service is active.
The front end is served by public and calls its /api routes.
The search route that public serves calls retrieval's search with the purpose embedding endpoint.
The routes that public serves call generation to grade candidates, write answers and translate.
public reads published navigation files from its read-only navigation mount.
The navigation builder extracts each book with extract_book before it writes the navigation file.
The label suggestions call retrieval's search for the wider list.
documentation keeps docs/claims.json at version 1 of the claims schema that Factory provides.
Factory's docs-verify reads this repository's docs/claims.json, whose cited paths and lines the link test checks.
